thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated inference latency detected for hosted-api (us-east-1). 90th/99th p50 increased. Pager triggered for oncall.

alice (oncall): acked. I'm on it. linking war-room when ready.

ben (sre): thanks — quick ask: any customer-facing errors? metrics show 5xx rate slightly up for /v1/generate.

carla (ic): initial triage: impact: increased response times and some 504s to a subset of API keys. Potentially hitting batching backlog. Notified Dedicated owners via DM.

dan (support): flagged top 3 customers on the watchlist: acme-inc, novella, edu-platform. I'll prep support thread.

alice (oncall): war room: https://warroom.redwood.internal/r/INC-2771234567 (Zoom + shared doc). Owner: ben (SRE).

ben (sre): I'm taking ownership. first steps: toggle canary fallback to lower-latency model, and drain long-lived worker queues. running command now:

```
# fallback to smaller model variant
redwoodctl rollout set --route hosted-api --model rdm-legacy-3b-quant --priority canary
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/kv-cache --replicas=0
```

ben (sre): applied canary fallback. backend reports immediate drop in p99 for canary traffic. Continuing to look at batching queues.

incident-bot: PAGE: PagerDuty incident PD-8357 dispatched to oncall.

carla (ic): Confirming handoff checklist: owner assigned, war room up, paging verified, customer impact assessment draft below. Please confirm who posts the public status page update.

alice (oncall): I can post the status page update. Draft below — please approve or edit.

alice (oncall): [DRAFT STATUS PAGE ENTRY]
- Summary: We are investigating increased request latency and intermittent 504 errors for the Redwood hosted inference API (us-east-1).
- Impact: Some customers experience slower responses and occasional request failures. A subset of high-throughput requests may be delayed.
- Mitigation: We have routed a portion of traffic to a lower-latency model variant and are draining backlog queues. Engineers are actively restoring normal throughput.
- ETA: next update in 15 minutes.

ben (sre): minor edit: add that Dedicated reserved pools are not impacted unless explicitly routed through hosted-api. Also add that we're prioritizing customer keys with highest error rates.

alice (oncall): updated. New draft appended.

alice (oncall): [STATUS PAGE DRAFT v2]
- Summary: We are investigating increased latency and intermittent request failures affecting the hosted inference API in us-east-1.
- Impact: Affected requests may see slower responses or occasional 504s. Dedicated deployments remain unaffected unless routed through the hosted endpoint.
- Mitigation: Traffic partially routed to a lower-latency model variant; backlog queues are being drained and additional capacity is being provisioned.
- What we're doing: SREs are draining long-lived workers, adjusting batching windows, and scaling temporary capacity.
- ETA: follow-up update at +15m, estimated recovery within 30-60 minutes depending on backlog drain.

carla (ic): approved. alice, please publish to status.redwood.ai and paste the link here. Also prepare a short customer notification to send to impacted customer contacts (support will handle distribution).

alice (oncall): publishing now... done: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2771234567

dan (support): drafting customer email for high-touch accounts. please review: 

```
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood hosted inference (us-east-1)

Hi <CUSTOMER_NAME>,

We're currently investigating elevated latency and intermittent request failures for the Redwood hosted inference API in us-east-1. Our engineers have routed a portion of traffic to a lower-latency model variant and are actively draining backlog queues. You may notice slower responses or occasional 504s.

We estimate normal service to return within 30-60 minutes, and we'll send another update in 15 minutes. If you rely on reserved Dedicated capacity, you should not be impacted unless your traffic goes through the hosted endpoint.

Apologies for the disruption — we're focused on restoring full performance.

Sincerely,
Redwood Support
```

carla (ic): looks good. dan, add a line about temporary rate-limit workarounds if they contact us for immediate relief.

ben (sre): current findings: KV cache pressure + a slow model kernel causing token generation stalls for long sequences. Workaround: reduce max_tokens for long-running requests and enable prefix caching for eligible requests. Patching kernels in progress.

alice (oncall): confirming paging chain: next if unack in 5m -> escalate to senior oncall (mike). if recovery not achieved in 30m -> paging to Eng Runtime lead.

ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK CHECK: confirmed steps executed: fallback rollout, queue drain initiated, status page posted. Suggested next step: temporarily lower default batching window to 30ms.

ben (sre): lowering batching window now via runtime cfg: `runtime.cfg.batch_window_ms=30`

ben (sre): improvements visible — p99 trending down. continuing to monitor.

alice (oncall): all good for now. keep war room open for 60m. ben, you continue as owner until we RC. carla will coordinate comms. dan will follow up on customer notifications and log all affected keys.

carla (ic): documented postmortem ownership in doc and created action items: long-term: kernel optimization, better backpressure controls, improved customer-targeted routing.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress; next update scheduled in 15 minutes.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone. closing initial kickoff thread — updates will roll into the war room and status page.
